seoTitle: Stripe Instant Payouts: Setup, Eligibility & Fees
metaDescription: Learn how to enable Stripe Instant Payouts, what eligibility requirements apply, and what fees you'll pay to move funds to your debit card in minutes.
intro: Instant Payouts let you move your Stripe balance to a linked debit card in minutes instead of waiting for a standard payout cycle, but there are eligibility rules and fees to understand first. This guide covers who qualifies, how to add and verify a debit card, what the fees look like, and how to activate the feature in your dashboard.

steps.heading: Check eligibility requirements
steps.body: Not every account or country qualifies for Instant Payouts, so confirm your account type meets the requirements before trying to enable it.

steps.heading: Add and verify your debit card
steps.body: Instant Payouts require a linked debit card, and Stripe will need to verify it before you can use the feature.

steps.heading: Understand fees and transfer timelines
steps.body: Instant Payouts typically carry a fee per transfer in exchange for the speed, so weigh that cost against how urgently you need the funds.

steps.heading: Activate Instant Payouts in Stripe
steps.body: Once eligibility and your debit card are confirmed, you can turn on Instant Payouts from your dashboard and start using it for future transfers.

faq.question: How fast are Stripe Instant Payouts?
faq.answer: Instant Payouts move your available balance to a linked debit card within minutes, rather than the several business days a standard payout can take.

faq.question: Do Instant Payouts cost extra?
faq.answer: Yes, Stripe charges a fee for each Instant Payout transfer, which is the tradeoff for getting funds faster.

faq.question: What do I need before I can use Instant Payouts?
faq.answer: You need an eligible account type and a verified debit card linked to your Stripe account before the feature becomes available.

faq.question: Can any Stripe account enable Instant Payouts?
faq.answer: No, eligibility depends on your account type and location, so it's worth checking the requirements before assuming the feature is available to you.
